title: row12
live_proof: inspection in the 3.22.0 tree: fts5CursorParseRank aliases the config strings (pCsr->zRank = pConfig->zRank, pCsr->zRankArgs = pConfig->zRankArgs) rather than copying them, and sqlite3Fts5ConfigLoad later sqlite3_free()s both. Fixed upstream in 3.43.2 by hoisting the reload above the rank parsing
object: pConfig->zRank and pConfig->zRankArgs, aliased by the cursor rather than copied
lifetime_ender: another connection redefines rank, the schema cookie bumps, and sqlite3Fts5ConfigLoad frees the strings the live cursor still aliases
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator. Two constraints are load-bearing. It needs two connections on one database, so it builds in the fts5S group with -USQLITE_OMIT_SHARED_CACHE and opens file::memory:?cache=shared -- a :memory: database takes SQLite's memDb path and never calls the VFS xOpen, which in this domain always returns SQLITE_CANTOPEN. And the rank weights are integers because the Capstone arm compiles with -DSQLITE_OMIT_FLOATING_POINT, under which 10.0 tokenizes as an integer followed by a stray dot; upstream's bm25(10.0,1.0) fails to parse there and every rank query returns a syntax error, which is how this case first came back reaching nothing
